parts.transcript: Part 2. Farm manager at Parson's Fruit Farm. Accommodation: motel is conveniently located just minutes away (B). Weather pretty mixed, forecasts always wrong (C). Tractor drivers must have a relevant permit/document from their country allowing them to operate the vehicle (A). Shed has heavy machinery so wear ear protection - noisy (B); shed is air conditioned. Final advice: have snacks and use water bottles often, people get exhausted quickly (A). Map: workshop accessed off the orchard road (G); lunchroom halfway round the bend by river and wood (B); farm office is the smallest building on south of main yard (H); first aid room attached to farmhouse in middle (F); store shed north past farmhouse, turn right before vegetable gardens (C).

parts.transcript: Part 3. Liz (NZ) and Scott (UK) plan a presentation on Stone Point, an extinct volcanic cone. Historical role: used by Maori and Europeans to shelter from or launch attack (A). Maori first attracted by fishing opportunities, soil benefits realised later (B). Agree to keep most Maori terminology out as international students couldn't follow (C). On the engines, Liz says don't go into the technical side, focus on impact on people's lives (A). To-do: Early Maori inhabitation - check who the writers were and when (D); lookout point - locate drawings/images of ships (B); reconstruction of fort - add more information/description about what prisoners added (A); modernisation 1930s-40s - ring Department of Conservation for agreement to film the site (F); 1950s onwards - arrange a meeting/interview about restoration work (C); public park - check where the boundary/location exactly is (E).

parts.title: Jatropha: a new biofuel
parts.transcript: Part 4. Lecture on Jatropha as a biofuel. Native to Central America. Survives in very poor quality infertile soil (31 soil). Resistant to drought for up to three years (32 drought). Prevents erosion (33 erosion). Seeds yield four times the oil of soybean and ten times that of corn (34 corn). In Africa used for water pumps and fridges, made into candles (35 candles), used as fencing; boiled leaves treat malaria (36 leaves); seeds treat digestion problems (37 digestion). European companies claim it ends rural poverty, works in current diesel engines, and the plants absorb great amounts of carbon dioxide when growing (38 carbon dioxide). Problems: some seeds toxic; oil productivity unreliable. Biofuels criticised for high food prices, loss of rainforest and disappearance of wildlife (39 wildlife), and contributing to global warming (40 global warming).
